t: 2767. Partition String Into Minimum Beautiful Substrings
o: Split binary string s into the fewest pieces where each piece has no leading zero and equals a power of 5 in binary (1, 101, 11001, 111101, ...). "1011" → "101"+"1" (2 pieces); "111" needs three "1"s; "0" is impossible (leading zero / not a power of 5). Length ≤ 15 means there are only 3 relevant powers of 5 (5⁰..5² fit in 15 bits; 5³=125 needs 7 bits — actually powers up to 5⁶ = 15625 = 11110100001001₂ fit), so we can precompute their binary forms in a set and DP over cut positions.
k: Precompute binary strings of 5⁰, 5¹, ... up to length 15 into a hash set.
dp[i] = min pieces for prefix of length i; dp[i] = min(dp[j]+1) over j where s[j:i] is beautiful.
Substring must start with '1' and be found in the power set.

a.n: Approach 1: Bottom-up DP with precomputed powers
a.i: Generate all powers of 5 whose binary representation has ≤ 15 bits, store in a set. Then for each position i, try every j < i with s[j]=='1' and s[j:i] in the set.
s: dp[0]=0; for i in 1..n try all j.
a.t: O(n²) substring checks (n ≤ 15) with O(1) hashing — effectively constant.
a.sp: O(n) DP plus the tiny power set.

a.i: Same recurrence expressed recursively: solve(i) = min over valid last-piece starts j of solve(j)+1. Equally fast; some find it easier to write.
s: Define solve(i) = min pieces for suffix starting at i.
Try each j > i with s[i]=='1' and s[i:j] a power of 5.

w: Either version is fine at n ≤ 15. Pitfalls: forgetting that '0' alone (or any piece starting with '0') is invalid — always require the first character '1'; and generating enough powers (5⁶ needs 14 bits). Follow-up: count the number of minimum partitions, or handle lengths up to 10⁵ (then parse values numerically with care for overflow, still O(n · #powers)).
